name: PE / PE32+
description: Windows executable and DLL format. Starts with MZ, e_lfanew at offset 0x3C points to the PE signature, the COFF header carries the machine type and the optional header carries the image base and subsystem.
limitations: Packed or protected binaries hide imports and sections
Managed .NET assemblies use the CLR data directory

name: ELF
description: Unix executable, shared object and object format. Magic 0x7F ELF, class byte selects 32/64-bit, e_machine identifies the architecture.
limitations: Stripped binaries lose symbol names
Android uses bionic-specific dynamic linking details

name: Mach-O
description: Apple executable format. Magic 0xFEEDFACE (32-bit), 0xFEEDFACF (64-bit), 0xCAFEBABE (universal/fat). Contains load commands including LC_BUILD_VERSION and LC_MAIN.
limitations: Fat binaries contain multiple slices
Code signing blobs add size and complexity

name: APK
description: Android application package: a ZIP containing AndroidManifest.xml in binary XML, classes.dex files, resources.arsc, res/ and lib/<abi>/*.so.
requirements: Binary XML parser for the manifest
limitations: Manifest is binary XML, not plain text
Signature scheme v2/v3 data lives outside the ZIP entries
Split APKs distribute code across multiple files

name: Android App Bundle
description: Publishing format containing modules, each with a manifest and dex, plus BundleConfig.pb. Google Play generates per-device APKs from it.
limitations: Cannot be installed directly on a device
Needs bundletool and a signing key
Module structure is more complex than an APK

name: Dalvik Executable (DEX)
description: Android bytecode container. Magic is dex\n followed by a three-digit version and a NUL byte, then header offsets and the string/type/method tables.
limitations: Multidex splits classes across files
Obfuscation removes readable names
Native code is referenced, not contained

name: Unity AssetBundle
description: Unity's packaged asset container. Starts with the ASCII magic UnityFS followed by a version, unityVersion and unityRevision string, then compressed blocks.
requirements: LZ4 or LZMA decompressor for block data
limitations: Serialized file layout is version-specific
Type trees may be stripped, complicating asset extraction
AssetBundles are engine-version locked

name: Unity global-metadata.dat
description: IL2CPP metadata file used to resolve managed type and method names in Unity builds. Magic 0xFAB11BAF (little-endian bytes AF 1B B1 FA), followed by a version and table offsets.
requirements: Binary reader for the metadata header
limitations: Version-specific table layout
Encrypted or obfuscated metadata is out of scope
Symbol recovery needs the matching binary

name: Unreal .uasset / .umap
description: Unreal Engine cooked asset package. Starts with the package file tag 0xC1832A9E, followed by legacy and UE4/UE5 version fields and a name table.
requirements: Matching engine version for property layout
limitations: Cooked packages are platform- and version-specific
Property serialization depends on the engine build
Encrypted packages are out of scope

name: Unreal .pak
description: Unreal's archive format for cooked content. The footer at the end of the file carries magic 0x5A6F12E1, the version, index offset and index size.
requirements: Footer scan from the end of the file
limitations: Footer size and layout vary by version
Encrypted pak files are out of scope
Index may be compressed

name: Godot .pck
description: Godot resource pack. Godot 3 starts with GDPC; Godot 4 uses the same magic with a different header layout and optional encryption.
requirements: Engine version from the pack header
limitations: Encrypted packs are out of scope
Resource formats are engine-version specific
PCK can be embedded in the executable

name: GameMaker data.win
description: GameMaker compiled game data. RIFF-like structure starting with FORM, a little-endian size, then GEN8, followed by a chunk table.
limitations: Format varies across GameMaker runtime versions
Bytecode is not source code
Assets are embedded in a proprietary layout

name: Ren'Py .rpa archive
description: Ren'Py asset archive. Header starts with RPA-3.0 or RPA-4.0 followed by the index offset and a XOR key, then a zlib-compressed pickled index.
requirements: zlib and a restricted pickle reader for the index
limitations: Pickle index must be read safely, never unpickled blindly
Encrypted archives are out of scope
Only assets, not game logic

name: LÖVE .love archive
description: A .love file is a ZIP archive containing main.lua, optional conf.lua and assets. The Android runtime loads it as the game source.
limitations: Compiled Lua bytecode may be present
No standard asset manifest
Not a native binary format

name: ISO 9660 / disc image
description: Optical disc filesystem used by console and PC disc images. The primary volume descriptor carries CD001 at offset 0x8001.
requirements: Filesystem parser for the specific disc format
limitations: Many console discs use custom filesystems on top
Encrypted or protected discs are out of scope
Large images need streaming reads

name: ZIP
description: Deflate-based archive format. Local file headers start with PK\x03\x04, the central directory with PK\x01\x02 and the end record with PK\x05\x06.
limitations: Data descriptors can hide sizes in local headers
Encrypted entries are out of scope
Zip64 fields differ from the classic layout

name: Ogg
description: Container format for Vorbis and Opus audio. Pages start with the ASCII magic OggS followed by a version byte and header flags.
limitations: Chained streams need per-stream handling
Seeking requires a granule-position index

name: WebAssembly module
description: Binary instruction format starting with the magic bytes 00 61 73 6D and a version word. Used by web builds and some engines as a scripting backend.
limitations: No direct Android system API access
Needs a host embedding layer
Not a native ARM binary

name: SQLite database
description: Embedded SQL database file. Header magic is SQLite format 3 followed by a NUL byte, page size and file change counters.
limitations: WAL files hold uncommitted state
Encrypted databases are out of scope
